name: Filtration-Width Splicing and Functoriality
statement: For every nonempty filtration $C_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq C_m$, $w(C_0,\ldots,C_m)=\max(\{\sigma(C_0)\}\cup\{\sigma(C_j;C_{j-1}):1\leq j\leq m\})$. Deleting prescribed stages cannot increase the width. Applying one pc-minor to every stage cannot increase it when the first resulting stage is nonempty. For equal-length filtrations on disjoint coordinates, synchronized products satisfy $w(C_0\times D_0,\ldots,C_m\times D_m)=\max\{w(C_0,\ldots,C_m),w(D_0,\ldots,D_m)\}$.
proof: Every admissible order restricts at stage $j$ to a $C_{j-1}$-first order of $C_j$, giving all lower bounds. Conversely, start with an optimal order of $C_0$ and at each stage append the new concepts in their order from an optimal $C_{j-1}$-first order of $C_j$; all of $C_{j-1}$ is already present, so the previous internal order is irrelevant to new step costs. Stage deletion relaxes constraints, and the minor and synchronized-product formulas follow termwise from the paired-width laws.
